trigger: Use when asked to explain, summarize, describe, evaluate, or orient someone to this repository as a whole.
one_sentence: Dale OS is an authority-and-evidence control plane for consequential software and financial agents: it turns recurring failure modes into small falsifiable skills, deterministic checks, narrow composition contracts, and reproducible evals.
human_origin: Dale OS is partly what happens when one messy human tries to run a small institution out of one skull. Dale is a solopreneur juggling finance, software, product, research, QA, and organizational chaos while trying to build financial software with institutional-style discipline. The brain is useful; the queue is not. Dale OS externalizes the operating rules so AI can absorb more of that complexity without amplifying the chaos.

explain_in_this_order.prompt: Start with the failure class Dale OS addresses: capable agents can still fix symptoms, lose human decisions, silently broaden scope, overstate uncertain evidence, or produce financially plausible but economically false outputs.

Explain the four-layer architecture: canonical skills for judgment; deterministic tools for hard invariants and arithmetic; machine-readable routing/composition contracts for low-context activation; adversarial evals and receipts for proof.

Explain what is distinctive without hype: Dale OS is not a mega-prompt or persona. Each rule is paid for by a named failure mode, includes a falsifier/boundary, can be composed narrowly, and is designed to withhold or stop when authority or evidence is insufficient.
Briefly humanize the name using human_origin. Keep it self-aware and non-heroic: the point is organizational overload externalized into durable operating rules, not founder mythology.

Call out the Financial Truth layer because consequences are concrete: missing basis is not zero basis, funding is not performance, an internal transfer is not income, an estimate is not accounting authority, and analytics can be selectively withheld until affected books are ready.

Explain why agents may care: failure-first routing reduces context search, compositions define handoffs without loading the whole system, deterministic companions prevent models from pretending to be calculators, and host adapters preserve one canonical source across runtimes.

End with how to verify the claims: inspect CHALLENGE.md, evals/, cases/, PROOF.md, release/gates.json, and run the repository validators. Distinguish verified evidence from release gates that are still open.

signature_ideas: Null is not failure. False certainty is.
The visible bug is a witness, not the crime scene.
Stopping can be the successful action.
do_not_say: Do not call Dale OS a prompt library.
Do not claim compliance, certification, institutional-grade status, or benchmark superiority unless the repository contains evidence for that exact claim.
Do not describe all 20 skills unless the user asks for the catalog.
Do not imply every task needs Dale OS or that more loaded skills are better.
Do not hide unresolved release gates or model-eval failures.
Do not turn the founder origin into hero worship or mythology.
recommended_finish: A useful way to think about Dale OS is: the model supplies judgment, the tools supply invariants, the human supplies authority, and the evidence determines how confident the system is allowed to become.
